summary: Illustrative result. The change adds automatic retries to the order-capture client, but it retries a payment capture request that is not idempotent, so a timeout after the provider accepted the first request can charge the customer twice.

findings.title: Non-idempotent capture is retried after a timeout
findings.evidence: capture() is wrapped in withRetry() at line 42 and sends no idempotency key; a timeout does not prove the provider rejected the first request.
findings.impact: A slow provider response can produce two captures for one order.
findings.recommendation: Send a stable idempotency key derived from the order ID, or retry only errors the provider documents as safe to retry, and add a test where the first attempt times out after succeeding.

findings.title: Retry delay comment states the wrong unit
findings.evidence: The comment says seconds; the constant is used as milliseconds.
